title.en: Enzymes: nature and mechanism of action

heading.en: A reaction ten million times faster

hook.en: Without an enzyme, carbon dioxide and water form about 200 molecules of carbonic acid per hour. With carbonic anhydrase, about 600,000 form every second.
hook.kn: ಕಿಣ್ವವಿಲ್ಲದೆ ಗಂಟೆಗೆ ಸುಮಾರು 200 ಕಾರ್ಬಾನಿಕ್ ಆಮ್ಲದ ಅಣುಗಳು ಉಂಟಾಗುತ್ತವೆ. ಕಾರ್ಬಾನಿಕ್ ಅನ್‌ಹೈಡ್ರೇಸ್ ಇದ್ದರೆ ಪ್ರತಿ ಸೆಕೆಂಡಿಗೆ ಸುಮಾರು 6 ಲಕ್ಷ ಅಣುಗಳು ಉಂಟಾಗುತ್ತವೆ.

objectives.en: State the chemical nature of enzymes.
Explain activation energy and how enzymes lower it.
Describe the enzyme–substrate complex and the catalytic cycle.

narration.en: Without an enzyme, carbon dioxide and water form about 200 molecules of carbonic acid per hour. With carbonic anhydrase, about 600,000 form every second.
narration.kn: ಕಿಣ್ವವಿಲ್ಲದೆ ಗಂಟೆಗೆ ಸುಮಾರು 200 ಕಾರ್ಬಾನಿಕ್ ಆಮ್ಲದ ಅಣುಗಳು ಉಂಟಾಗುತ್ತವೆ. ಕಾರ್ಬಾನಿಕ್ ಅನ್‌ಹೈಡ್ರೇಸ್ ಇದ್ದರೆ ಪ್ರತಿ ಸೆಕೆಂಡಿಗೆ ಸುಮಾರು 6 ಲಕ್ಷ ಅಣುಗಳು ಉಂಟಾಗುತ್ತವೆ.

body.en: Almost all enzymes are proteins; some nucleic acids that behave like enzymes are called ribozymes. An enzyme, like any protein, has a tertiary structure with crevices or pockets; one such pocket where the substrate fits is the active site. Unlike inorganic catalysts, enzymes are damaged at high temperatures (above 40 °C), though enzymes from thermophilic organisms living at 80–90 °C stay stable. Carbonic anhydrase speeds up the reaction CO₂ + H₂O → H₂CO₃ about 10 million times.

points.en: Ribozymes: nucleic acids with enzyme activity.
Active site: the pocket into which the substrate fits.
Enzymes are not used up in the reaction.

narration.kn: ಬಹುತೇಕ ಎಲ್ಲ ಕಿಣ್ವಗಳು ಪ್ರೋಟೀನ್‌ಗಳು; ಕಿಣ್ವದಂತೆ ವರ್ತಿಸುವ ನ್ಯೂಕ್ಲಿಯಿಕ್ ಆಮ್ಲಗಳನ್ನು ರೈಬೋಜೈಮ್ ಎನ್ನುತ್ತಾರೆ. ಕಿಣ್ವದ ಸಕ್ರಿಯ ತಾಣದಲ್ಲಿ ಆಧಾರವಸ್ತು ಕೂರುತ್ತದೆ.

body.en: A substrate must reach a higher-energy transition state before it becomes product. The energy needed to reach it is the activation energy. Enzymes lower the activation energy, so the reaction goes faster; they do not change the energy difference between substrate and product. The enzyme binds the substrate (S) at its active site to form a short-lived enzyme–substrate complex (ES), which changes into an enzyme–product complex (EP) and releases the product, freeing the enzyme for another substrate molecule.

points.en: E + S ⇌ ES → EP → E + P
Lower activation energy means a faster reaction.

problem.en: Without the enzyme about 200 molecules of H₂CO₃ form in an hour; with carbonic anhydrase about 600,000 form every second. Estimate how many times faster the catalysed reaction is.

steps.en: Uncatalysed rate: 200 per hour = 200 ÷ 3600 ≈ 0.056 molecules per second.
